analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and rewrites the `stop` row of the sampling-parameters table (line 2122). The row now says Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning and tool-call spans from stop-string matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`). It also says the native block engine matches the whole output and carries no scope. No source code, config, key handling, attestation, or coordinator contract is modified, so no executable security behavior changes in this diff. I examined the base text excerpts (lines 1643-2462) for context on the surrounding stop-string, MTP, deadline, and reasoning-parser documentation. I found nothing that makes the new row contradict a documented security control. Relevant assets and threats are A-001 and the TB-007 inference engine. Stop-string scoping affects output truncation, not confidentiality, encryption, authorization, or billing boundaries as documented. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is not touched. Open integration question: the documented `ReasoningStopScope` behavior is implemented in code outside this batch (`EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`). Whether stop strings can match inside hidden reasoning or tool-call text and cut or leak output is a correctness matter I could not verify from the supplied evidence, and I do not claim it as a vulnerability. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation-only change.
